# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Qiao_2026_imipenem"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Qiao_2026_imipenem"))$description`
* Article: [Drug Des Devel Ther. 2026;20:606942](https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S606942)

# Population

Forty-six critically ill adults in the intensive care unit of Chongqing
University Central Hospital (China), enrolled January to December 2025, who
received imipenem-cilastatin together with continuous renal replacement therapy
(CRRT) for at least 24 h. The cohort was 52.2% male, median age 68 years (range
18-96) and median weight 60 kg (range 35-85); 40 patients (87%) had sepsis or
septic shock and 17 (37%) acute kidney injury (Table 1).

CRRT was continuous veno-venous hemofiltration (CVVH) in 38 patients and
haemodiafiltration (CVVHDF) in 8, with a median blood flow of 150 mL/min
(115-200) and a median ultrafiltration flow of 2362 mL/h (2029-3840). The
Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance, computed from serum creatinine measured
during CRRT, had a median of 40.07 mL/min and spanned 6.70-157.98 mL/min, so the
cohort includes patients whose native renal function was recovering. The
per-patient CRRT clearance of imipenem, calculated from the circuit flows and
the measured effluent-to-plasma concentration ratio, had a median of 2.48 L/h
(1.37-3.72).

Patients received 0.5 g every 6 h (22 patients) or 1 g every 8 h (24 patients)
as a 2-h intravenous infusion. 560 plasma samples (plus 280 effluent samples)
were drawn pre-dose and 0.5-8 h after a dose at or near steady state.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Qiao_2026_imipenem")()$population`).

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Qiao_2026_imipenem.R`. The table below
collects them in one place for review.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment model, linear elimination | n/a | Results, "PopPK Model"; Discussion |
| `CL_TOTAL = 6.08 * (CrCl / 40.07)^0.383 * exp(eta_CL) + CL_CRRT` | n/a | Equation 10 |
| `CL_CVVH = SC * Q_E * [Q_b / (Q_b + Q_R)] / 1000`; `CL_CVVHDF` the same with SA | n/a | Equations 1-5 |
| Exponential IIV, `eta ~ N(0, omega^2)` | n/a | Equation 6 |
| Proportional residual error, `Y = IPRED * (1 + eps)` | n/a | Equation 7 |
| `lcl` | 6.08 L/h (RSE 7%) | Table 2, final model |
| `lvc` (V1) | 24.4 L (RSE 9%) | Table 2, final model |
| `lq` (Q) | 3.19 L/h (RSE 30%) | Table 2, final model |
| `lvp` (V2) | 12.0 L (RSE 36%) | Table 2, final model |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.383 (RSE 26%) | Table 2 row 'CLCR-CL'; Equation 10 |
| `CRCL` centring constant | 40.07 mL/min (cohort median) | Equation 10; Table 1 |
| `etalcl` | omega^2 = 0.192 (RSE 29%) | Table 2 row 'IIV-CL' |
| `etalvc` | omega^2 = 0.161 (RSE 36%) | Table 2 row 'IIV-V1' |
| `propSd` | sqrt(0.0849) = 0.291 | Table 2 row 'PROB-erro' (sigma^2) |
| Screened, not retained | WT, AGE, ALT, BUN, RBC, neutrophil %, septic shock | Supplementary Table S1 |

## Covariates the user must supply

* `CRCL` - Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance in mL/min (not normalised to
  body surface area), with serum creatinine in umol/L and the 0.818 divisor of
  the Table 1 footnote.
* `QEFF` - the patient's CRRT clearance of imipenem in L/h, added to the
  endogenous clearance outside the random effect. The paper computes it from
  the effluent flow, the predilution correction and the measured sieving
  (CVVH) or saturation (CVVHDF) coefficient; it does not report those
  coefficients.

# Virtual cohort

Original observed data are not publicly available. The cohort below mirrors
the two administered regimens, 200 virtual patients per regimen. Creatinine
clearance is drawn log-normally around the 40.07 mL/min median and truncated
to the observed 6.70-157.98 mL/min range; CRRT clearance is drawn normally
around the 2.48 L/h median and truncated to the observed 1.37-3.72 L/h range.
The spreads of both distributions are chosen by the maintainers to fill the
reported ranges, because Table 1 gives only medians and ranges.

```{r cohort}
# rxode2's simulation RNG is partitioned per solver thread, so the drawn
# cohort is not reproducible across machines with different thread counts.
# Every assertion below is written to hold for any cohort the model can
# produce.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260824)
set.seed(20260824)

mod <- readModelDb("Qiao_2026_imipenem")

N_PER_ARM <- 200L

rtrunc <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  x <- draw(n)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- draw(sum(bad))
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

observed_regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,     ~amt, ~ii,
  "0.5 g q6h",   500,   6,
  "1 g q8h",    1000,   8
)

# One steady-state dosing interval per patient (`ss = 1`), 2-h infusion as
# administered (Methods, "Patients and Medications"), observed on a 0.1-h grid.
make_obs_arm <- function(amt, ii, regimen, id_offset) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = amt, dur = 2, ii = ii, ss = 1, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(round(seq(0, ii, by = 0.1), 6), cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(id = seq_len(N_PER_ARM))
  as.data.frame(ev) |>
    # `.env$ii`: the event table has its own `ii` column (NA on observation
    # rows), which a bare `ii` would pick up instead of the argument.
    dplyr::mutate(id = id + id_offset, regimen = regimen, tau = .env$ii)
}

events_obs <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(observed_regimens)), function(i) {
  make_obs_arm(
    observed_regimens$amt[i], observed_regimens$ii[i],
    observed_regimens$regimen[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * N_PER_ARM
  )
}))

covs <- tibble::tibble(
  id = sort(unique(events_obs$id)),
  CRCL = rtrunc(length(id), function(n) rlnorm(n, log(40.07), 0.75), 6.70, 157.98),
  QEFF = rtrunc(length(id), function(n) rnorm(n, 2.48, 0.55), 1.37, 3.72)
)
events_obs <- dplyr::left_join(events_obs, covs, by = "id")

summary(covs[, c("CRCL", "QEFF")])
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate-obs}
sim_obs <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_obs, returnType = "data.frame",
                           maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(events_obs, id, regimen, tau), by = "id")
```

## Concentration-time profiles

```{r profiles}
pi_obs <- sim_obs |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(sim)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.10), p50 = median(sim), p90 = quantile(sim, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(pi_obs, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Imipenem plasma concentration (mg/L)",
       title = "Simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles (with residual error)",
       caption = "Compare with the VPC of Figure 3 of Qiao 2026.")
```

Figure 3 of the paper is a VPC of the plasma data against time since the first
dose. Read off the figure, the observed median lies between about 7.5 and 16
mg/L, the observed 10th percentile near 2 mg/L and the observed 90th
percentile between about 31 and 41 mg/L, while the simulated 90th-percentile
confidence band reaches down to about 19-25 mg/L. The check below pools the
simulated concentrations at the paper's sampling times (pre-dose and 0.5-8 h
after a dose, Methods) across both regimens. The pooled median falls on the
observed one; the simulated upper percentile sits a little below the observed
one, which depends on the creatinine- and CRRT-clearance spreads assumed for
the virtual cohort (Table 1 gives only medians and ranges).

```{r vpc-check}
sample_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8)
pooled <- sim_obs |>
  dplyr::filter(round(time, 6) %in% sample_times, time <= tau, !is.na(sim))
vpc_q <- quantile(pooled$sim, c(0.10, 0.50, 0.90))
round(vpc_q, 2)

stopifnot(
  # Structural: Css,avg is Dose / (tau * CL), so a mis-transcribed CL, V1,
  # dose or unit moves the pooled median by tens of percent.
  vpc_q[["50%"]] > 6, vpc_q[["50%"]] < 18,
  # Envelope, read from Figure 3 with headroom for the digitising error and
  # the cohort draw.
  vpc_q[["10%"]] > 0.5, vpc_q[["10%"]] < 5,
  vpc_q[["90%"]] > 20, vpc_q[["90%"]] < 50
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no non-compartmental results, so the NCA below is checked
against the steady-state identity `AUC0-tau,ss = Dose / CL`, which must hold
for each simulated patient whatever its parameters.

```{r pknca, message = FALSE}
conc_nca <- sim_obs |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, time, Cc)

dose_nca <- events_obs |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(amt), amt > 0) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, time, amt, tau)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | regimen + id)

intervals <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(regimen = "0.5 g q6h", start = 0, end = 6),
  data.frame(regimen = "1 g q8h", start = 0, end = 8)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)

nca_tab |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3),
    p10 = signif(quantile(PPORRES, 0.10), 3),
    p90 = signif(quantile(PPORRES, 0.90), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
                "Median" = median, "10th percentile" = p10, "90th percentile" = p90) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA (typical cohort, 2-h infusion).")
```

```{r pknca-identity}
cl_by_id <- sim_obs |> dplyr::distinct(id, cl)
auc_chk <- nca_tab |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(dose_nca, by = c("id", "regimen")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_by_id, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = PPORRES / (amt / cl))

summary(auc_chk$ratio)

# Both sides use the same drawn parameters, so the difference is linear-up /
# log-down trapezoid error on a 0.1-h grid plus integrator tolerance; it is
# below 0.2% for every patient in practice.
stopifnot(nrow(auc_chk) == 2L * N_PER_ARM, max(abs(auc_chk$ratio - 1)) < 0.01)
```

# Replicating the probability of target attainment (Figure 6)

The paper's Monte Carlo simulations (Methods, "Monte Carlo Simulations";
Figures 4-9) stratify by creatinine clearance (<= 30, 31-60, 61-90 and >= 90
mL/min), CRRT intensity (20, 37 and 74 mL/h/kg at the 60 kg median weight)
and modality, and score 40% fT>MIC at steady state for six regimens. Three
inputs needed to repeat them are not stated in the paper and are set here as
follows.

* **CRRT clearance per scenario.** The paper converts the CRRT dose to an
  imipenem clearance through Equations 4-5 but does not report the sieving or
  saturation coefficient, the blood flow or the replacement flow it used. Here
  `QEFF = CRRT dose x 60 kg / 1000` (L/h), i.e. the product of the sieving
  coefficient and the predilution factor is taken as 1. Applying the
  predilution factor at the median blood flow of 150 mL/min with a sieving
  coefficient of 1 lowers `QEFF` at 37 mL/h/kg from 2.22 to 1.78 L/h and
  roughly doubles the RMSE against the 24 digitised cells below (4.3 versus
  2.2 percentage points in a 1000-patient check).
* **Infusion duration.** The patients received 2-h infusions, but the
  published curves are reproduced only with a 0.5-h infusion; a 2-h infusion
  raises fT>MIC and overshoots the figure systematically (computed below).
* **Creatinine clearance within a band.** Each band is represented by a single
  value: 15, 45, 75 and 120 mL/min.

PTA is computed on total plasma concentration, as the model predicts it; the
paper applies no unbound-fraction correction.

```{r pta-setup}
pta_regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,     ~amt, ~ii,
  "0.5 g q6h",   500,   6,
  "0.5 g q8h",   500,   8,
  "0.5 g q12h",  500,  12,
  "1 g q6h",    1000,   6,
  "1 g q8h",    1000,   8,
  "1 g q12h",   1000,  12
)
crcl_bands <- tibble::tibble(
  band = factor(c("<= 30", "31-60", "61-90", ">= 90"),
                levels = c("<= 30", "31-60", "61-90", ">= 90")),
  CRCL = c(15, 45, 75, 120)
)
mic_grid <- c(0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32)
WT_SIM <- 60  # kg, Table 1 median; Results 'Simulations and Target Attainment'

pta_events <- function(regs, crrt_dose, dur) {
  arms <- tidyr::crossing(regs, crcl_bands)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(amt = arms$amt[i], dur = dur, ii = arms$ii[i], ss = 1, cmt = "central") |>
      rxode2::et(round(seq(0, arms$ii[i], by = 0.05), 6), cmt = "central") |>
      rxode2::et(id = seq_len(N_PER_ARM))
    as.data.frame(ev) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        id = id + (i - 1L) * N_PER_ARM,
        regimen = arms$regimen[i], tau = arms$ii[i], band = arms$band[i],
        CRCL = arms$CRCL[i], QEFF = crrt_dose * WT_SIM / 1000
      )
  }))
}

pta_from <- function(model, ev) {
  meta <- dplyr::distinct(ev, id, regimen, tau, band)
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
    dplyr::left_join(meta, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::filter(time < tau)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
  # Fraction of the dosing interval above each MIC, per patient; the grid is
  # uniform, so the fraction of grid points equals the fraction of time.
  ft <- sim |>
    dplyr::group_by(id, regimen, band) |>
    dplyr::reframe(MIC = mic_grid,
                   ft = vapply(mic_grid, function(m) mean(Cc > m), numeric(1)))
  ft |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen, band, MIC) |>
    dplyr::summarise(PTA = 100 * mean(ft >= 0.4), .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r pta-figure6, fig.height = 7}
pta37 <- pta_from(mod, pta_events(pta_regimens, crrt_dose = 37, dur = 0.5))

ggplot(pta37, aes(MIC, PTA, colour = band)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(50, 80, 90), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = mic_grid, labels = format(mic_grid)) +
  facet_wrap(~factor(regimen, levels = pta_regimens$regimen), ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA, 40% fT>MIC (%)", colour = "CrCl (mL/min)",
       title = "CVVH, 37 mL/h/kg",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Qiao 2026.") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

The table compares the simulated PTA for the three 0.5 g regimens at MIC 4
and 8 mg/L with values digitised by the maintainers from Figure 6 (panels A-C;
the 1 g panels D-F repeat them at twice the MIC, as linear kinetics require).

```{r pta-compare}
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,     ~MIC, ~`<= 30`, ~`31-60`, ~`61-90`, ~`>= 90`,
  "0.5 g q6h",     4,      100,       97,       93,       83,
  "0.5 g q8h",     4,       96,       86,       76,       57,
  "0.5 g q12h",    4,       75,       51,       35,       18,
  "0.5 g q6h",     8,       90,       68,       55,       37,
  "0.5 g q8h",     8,       67,       38,       23,       10,
  "0.5 g q12h",    8,       15,        4,        1,        0
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(regimen, MIC), names_to = "band", values_to = "published") |>
  dplyr::mutate(band = factor(band, levels = levels(crcl_bands$band)))

cmp37 <- fig6 |>
  dplyr::left_join(pta37, by = c("regimen", "band", "MIC")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = PTA - published)

cmp37 |>
  dplyr::arrange(MIC, regimen, band) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "MIC (mg/L)" = MIC, "CrCl band (mL/min)" = band,
                "Figure 6 PTA (%)" = published, "Simulated PTA (%)" = PTA,
                "Difference" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

rmse <- function(d) sqrt(mean(d^2))
c(RMSE = rmse(cmp37$diff), mean_bias = mean(cmp37$diff))
```

With 200 patients per arm the Monte Carlo standard error of one cell is up to
3.5 percentage points, and in a 1000-patient check this configuration lands
within an RMSE of 2.2 points of the digitised values. The gate below sits well
above that and well below the 12-13 points of the two rejected readings
(next sections).

```{r pta-gate}
stopifnot(nrow(cmp37) == 24L, !anyNA(cmp37$PTA),
          rmse(cmp37$diff) < 7, abs(mean(cmp37$diff)) < 5)
```

## Infusion duration of the simulations

```{r pta-2h, message = FALSE}
pta37_2h <- pta_from(mod, pta_events(dplyr::filter(pta_regimens, amt == 500),
                                     crrt_dose = 37, dur = 2))
cmp37_2h <- fig6 |>
  dplyr::left_join(pta37_2h, by = c("regimen", "band", "MIC")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = PTA - published)
c(RMSE = rmse(cmp37_2h$diff), mean_bias = mean(cmp37_2h$diff))
# The 2-h infusion overshoots by about 7.5 points on average (1000-patient
# check); the Monte Carlo standard error of a 24-cell mean is about 1 point,
# while the 0.5-h configuration above is gated at |bias| < 5.
stopifnot(mean(cmp37_2h$diff) > 4)
```

A 2-h infusion, as administered to the patients, overshoots the published
curves systematically (an RMSE of about 9 percentage points against about 3
for the 0.5-h infusion), so the published simulations evidently used a
shorter infusion; 0.5 h is the conventional one.

## Scale of the variance estimates in Table 2

Table 2 prints the inter-individual variability rows ('IIV-CL' 0.192, 'IIV-V1'
0.161) and the proportional residual row ('PROB-erro' 0.0849) without saying
whether they are variances or standard deviations. Methods (Equations 6-7)
define the random effects by their variances, which is what NONMEM reports.
Re-running the Figure 6 comparison with the two IIV values read as standard
deviations instead (variances 0.192^2 and 0.161^2) shows which reading the
paper's own simulations used.

```{r omega-scale, message = FALSE}
# 0.036864 = 0.192^2 and 0.025921 = 0.161^2.
mod_sd <- rxode2::rxode2(mod) |> rxode2::ini(etalcl ~ 0.036864, etalvc ~ 0.025921)
pta37_sd <- pta_from(mod_sd, pta_events(dplyr::filter(pta_regimens, amt == 500),
                                        crrt_dose = 37, dur = 0.5))
cmp37_sd <- fig6 |>
  dplyr::left_join(pta37_sd, by = c("regimen", "band", "MIC")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = PTA - published)

tibble::tibble(
  Reading = c("Variances (model)", "Standard deviations"),
  RMSE = c(rmse(cmp37$diff), rmse(cmp37_sd$diff))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "RMSE (percentage points) against the 24 digitised Figure 6 cells.")

stopifnot(rmse(cmp37_sd$diff) > rmse(cmp37$diff) + 4)
```

The standard-deviation reading makes the curves far too steep (for example
0.5 g q12h at MIC 4 mg/L and CrCl <= 30 mL/min gives about 97% against the
published 75%), so the model encodes the Table 2 values as variances, and the
residual row on the same scale (`propSd = sqrt(0.0849)`).

## Statements in the Results text at other CRRT intensities

```{r pta-claims}
claim_regs <- dplyr::filter(pta_regimens, regimen %in% c("1 g q6h", "1 g q8h"))
pta74 <- pta_from(mod, pta_events(claim_regs, crrt_dose = 74, dur = 0.5))
pta20 <- pta_from(mod, pta_events(claim_regs, crrt_dose = 20, dur = 0.5))

claims <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pta74 |> dplyr::filter(regimen == "1 g q6h", band == ">= 90", MIC == 8) |>
    dplyr::mutate(claim = "74 mL/h/kg, 1 g q6h, CrCl >= 90, MIC 8: 'approximately 70%'", published = 70),
  pta20 |> dplyr::filter(regimen == "1 g q6h", band == "<= 30", MIC == 16) |>
    dplyr::mutate(claim = "20 mL/h/kg, 1 g q6h, CrCl <= 30, MIC 16: '> 80%'", published = NA_real_),
  pta20 |> dplyr::filter(regimen == "1 g q8h", band == "<= 30", MIC == 16) |>
    dplyr::mutate(claim = "20 mL/h/kg, 1 g q8h, CrCl <= 30, MIC 16: 'approached 80%'", published = 80)
)
claims |>
  dplyr::select(claim, PTA) |>
  dplyr::rename("Results statement" = claim, "Simulated PTA (%)" = PTA) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  abs(claims$PTA[1] - 70) < 12,
  claims$PTA[2] > 80,
  abs(claims$PTA[3] - 80) < 12
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV and residual scale.** Table 2 does not label its variability rows. They
  are taken as NONMEM variances (omega^2, sigma^2), as Equations 6-7 define
  them; the standard-deviation reading is rejected by the Figure 6 comparison
  above.
* **Table 2 unit label.** The 'CLCR-CL' row is labelled L/h but is the
  dimensionless power exponent of Equation 10.
* **Serum creatinine unit.** The Table 1 footnote writes serum creatinine in
  mmol/L, but the tabulated values (median 126, range 34-673) and the 0.818
  divisor of the Cockcroft-Gault form are umol/L.
* **CRRT clearance.** `QEFF` is a per-patient input. The paper reports no
  sieving or saturation coefficient, so a user converting a prescribed CRRT
  dose must supply one; the PTA replication here uses `QEFF = CRRT dose x 60
  kg / 1000`, which reproduces Figure 6 more closely than applying the
  predilution correction at the median blood flow.
* **Simulated infusion duration.** 0.5 h in the PTA replication (not stated by
  the paper; the patients received 2-h infusions), because it reproduces the
  published curves and 2 h does not.
* **Creatinine clearance bands and cohort spreads.** Single representative
  values per band in the PTA replication; log-normal and normal spreads for
  creatinine clearance and CRRT clearance in the cohort simulation, chosen to
  fill the Table 1 ranges.
* **Modality.** CVVH and CVVHDF share one model; the paper reports nearly
  identical PTA for the two, and only CVVH (Figure 6) is replicated here.
* **Supplementary Table S1** (covariate screening) was retrieved from the
  publisher; it holds no parameter values used by the model.
* No erratum was found (Europe PMC, 2026-11-16).
